## 1. This week's analysis

Load in packages

```{r}
#install.packages("BiocManager")
#BiocManager::install("DESeq2")
library(DESeq2)
```




Load Reads

```{r}

counts_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobertsLab/paper-tanner-crab/master/analyses/kallisto-0812/kallisto-0812.isoform.counts.matrix"
counts <- read.delim(counts_url, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# kallisto gives estimated counts with decimals; DESeq2 needs whole numbers
counts <- round(counts)

dim(counts)   # 78,649 transcripts x 4 samples
head(counts)

```


> Reads are divided into four different catagories, cold_uninfected, cold_infected, warm_uninfected, and warm_infected with counts of how many counts are in each category at each site.  


Describe sample
Each row of the metadata describes one column of the count matrix, in the same order.

```{r}
coldata <- data.frame(
  row.names   = colnames(counts),
  infection   = factor(c("uninfected", "infected", "uninfected", "infected")),
  temperature = factor(c("cold", "cold", "warm", "warm"))
)
coldata

# Stop here if the names don't line up
stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata) == colnames(counts)))
```


> create count matrix  


Build the DESeq2 object

```{r}
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts,
                              colData   = coldata,
                              design    = ~ infection)

# Levels are alphabetical by default, so "infected" would be the reference.
# Make "uninfected" the baseline so a positive log2FoldChange means higher in infected crabs.
dds$infection <- relevel(dds$infection, ref = "uninfected")

# Drop transcripts with almost no reads
dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10, ]
nrow(dds)
```


> Number of counts left after removing counts with less than 10 reads  


Check sample structure
Do this before testing anything. Do the samples group by infection, by temperature, or by neither?

```{r}
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("infection", "temperature"))
```


> Infected_cold is further away from the other three categories on PC2 meaning it is more different from the rest of the counts in the category and uninfected war and infected cold oare closer on PC1 than the other two indicating that reads in those categories are more similar. 



Test for differential expression

```{r}
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds, alpha = 0.05)

summary(res)
sum(res$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)   # number of significant transcripts
```


> Out of 38,411 reads, 1,166 were significantly differentially expressed (p-value = 0.05). In LFC up 1,050 reads have higher expression when compared to the control. In LFC down 116 reads have lower expression when compared to the control. There are 0 outlier reads and 17,872 reads were cut from the counts becuase they had less than 10 reads.


PLot and save results

```{r}
plotMA(res, ylim = c(-10, 10), main = "Infected vs uninfected")

res_df <- as.data.frame(res)
res_df$transcript_id <- rownames(res_df)
res_df <- res_df[order(res_df$padj), ]
head(res_df)

dir.create("output/week04", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(res_df, "output/week04/dge-results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


> postive log fold change means there are higher reads for infected crabs and a negative log fold change means there are higher reads for uninfectd crabs. 


Write a caveats paragraph about design, sample size, and biological interpretation.

> Some caveats to this is that in a sample site you are more likely to get crabs in the same category than in both categories. Crabs live in close proximity to each other so and infected crab is more likey to get crabs in the vacinity infected. Another cavaet is that there were only four sites samples so it is hard to tell if there was a wide variety of crabs sampled.  



## 2. Reflection questions

<!-- The 2–3 questions from this week's lecture page, answered with reasoning. -->

1. Why is sample metadata as important as the count matrix?

> Count matrix tells us what we need to know about the read, like what type of read it is (ex:RNA or eDNA) along with how mny sequences are in that read for that category. The sample matrix is just as important because it provides context for where these reads come from and why they could be useful.  

2. What is the difference between statistical significance and biological importance in differential expression?

> Statistical significance is how likel you are to detect a true alternative to the null and is based on statistical equations whereas biological importance tells us what is happening in the environment.

3. If your project is not RNA-seq, what is the equivalent of a count matrix and a results table in your workflow?

> I am using eDNA so the equivalent of a count matrix would be a count matrix would be the number of reads per site and a result table would be how many of each species were at that site.
